bounds_notes: Nothing quantified. Follow-up (high expected value — PYF has ~280,000 people across 67 inhabited islands with very uneven network coverage, so this is one of the larger real gaps in the batch): locate the ISPF RP2022 housing tables or microdata by direct file URL, or request them from ISPF; https://www.ispf.pf/publication/1396 is the named publication landing page.

source: KAHRAMAA household-interview data, cited secondhand in 'Bottled water or filtered tap water? A nexus-based sustainability assessment for Qatar', J. Cleaner Production (2026)
mapping_notes: Nothing filled. Per rubric rule 6, the only figure is a tap-water-consumption attitude statistic ('only 30% of residents consume tap water') reported secondhand rather than a census main-drinking-source table, and the implied ~70% non-tap share lumps bottled, dispenser/cooler delivery and filtered water together - which straddles Packaged, Delivered and piped. Filling Packaged=70 from it would both violate rule 6 and mis-assign the Delivered component.
bounds_notes: Recorded but NOT filled: only ~30% of Qatar residents consume tap water (KAHRAMAA home interviews), implying up to ~70% rely primarily on bottled/other non-piped drinking water; 68.02% of university students prefer bottled (non-representative). Cooler-bottle home delivery (Delivered) is likely embedded in that ~70% and is not broken out. Population essentially fully urban. Follow-up: Qatar PSA Census 2020 / data.gov.qa - no water-source table located so far.

source: SISPEA (services.eaufrance.fr), 'Departement Reunion (974), 2023'
mapping_notes: Same treatment as Guadeloupe and Martinique. SISPEA 2023: 872,635 inhabitants across 46 services, compliance 95.8% / 98.4% — near-universal network connection, so Borehole, OtherUnpiped and Delivered are evidence-based zeros (rubric rule 3). The Coalition Eau claim that 46% of users are supplied by networks 'not guaranteeing satisfactory health safety' is explicitly NOT mapped to any of our columns: it is a water-QUALITY statement about network water, has no primary citation, and mapping it to OtherUnpiped would be a category error of nearly half the population. INSEE's housing-comfort table for Reunion (electricity 99.4%, hot water 93.2%, indoor bath/WC 98.2%) has no explicit running-water variable, so there is no household-level check available. Packaged left null — unmeasured. Single stratum, applied to both URBAN and RURAL.
bounds_notes: Recorded but NOT used: Coalition Eau's '46% of users on networks not guaranteeing satisfactory health safety' — unverified, no primary citation, and about quality rather than source type. If it were ever mis-mapped to OtherUnpiped it would be the single largest error in this batch. The zeros here are inferred from network coverage, not measured.

source: INS, Recensamantul Populatiei si Locuintelor 2021 (RPL2021), Table 8.7 'Locuinte conventionale dupa tipul cladirii si dotarea cu instalatii si dependinte, pe medii de rezidenta' (ref. 1 Dec 2021), n=7,692,147 (urban 4,359,365 / rural 3,332,782)
mapping_notes: The census category is 'alimentare cu apa in locuinta din SISTEM PROPRIU' - water PIPED INTO THE DWELLING from the household's OWN system. Mapped to Borehole, not OtherUnpiped: an own system that feeds in-dwelling plumbing necessarily involves a well plus a pump and pressure installation, which is exactly the rubric's Borehole definition (own drilled well with electric pump/hydrophore); a hand-drawn traditional dug well would show up as 'no installation', not as an own piped system. Urban 11.1 / rural 37.0 taken directly from the census urban/rural columns (no national_applied_to_both needed). Piped from public network (urban 89.6 / rural 44.7 / national 70.1) excluded as piped. Packaged and Delivered have no census category at all -> left null, not zero. The 6.4% national 'no water installation at all' figure is published without an urban/rural split and, critically, does not say what those households actually drink (could be a village street tap = piped, a hand-dug well, or a spring), so per rubric rule 4 I did NOT allocate it to OtherUnpiped. Caveat carried from the source: multiple answers were allowed, so the categories are not strictly mutually exclusive - urban 89.6 + 11.1 = 100.7, i.e. ~0.7pp of urban dwellings report both public and own supply and are double-counted here. | VERIFIER: values count own-system supply piped INSIDE the dwelling only; adding own-system outside dwelling (145,225 + 460,149 households) roughly doubles them, and the census table is multi-response. Treat 11.1/37.0 as a FLOOR.
bounds_notes: Unallocated residual: rural 100 - 44.7 - 37.0 = 18.3pp and national 6.4% 'no water installation' - this is the upper bound for RURALOtherUnpiped but its composition is unstated. Cross-checks: Eurostat 74.1% connected (2021) vs census 70.1% public network; press citing INS/ANRSC (2024) reports ~60% of rural residents on wells, well above the 37.0% own-piped-system figure, consistent with a large additional unpiped-well population sitting inside the 'no installation' residual.
verification: CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 vs RPL2021 Tabel 8.7/8.13 xlsx (22.32/37.01/11.08 exact)

source: St Helena Government Statistics Office, St Helena Population and Housing Census 2021 Main Report (July 2021), Table A18 (p.27) and Table B24 (p.61, by district).
mapping_notes: Census water-supply distribution (n=1,937 households): treated supply from Connect Saint Helena Ltd 92.1% (1,784) + untreated supply from Connect Saint Helena Ltd 6.6% (128) = 98.7% on the utility's piped network -> EXCLUDED as piped. Remaining 1.3% (25 households) = 'Other / rainwater tank / spring / stream' -> OtherUnpiped 1.3. Packaged, Delivered and Borehole set to 0 rather than null under rubric rule 3: the census response list is exhaustive and contains no bottled, tanker/vendor or well/borehole option, and any such household would have to sit inside the 1.3% 'other' line - i.e. each of the three is bounded above by 1.3% and there is no bottled-water utility, water-vendor trade or groundwater abstraction on the island. Rubric rule 1 caveat: this is a HOUSEHOLD SUPPLY question, not a drinking-specific one, so the 0s describe supply not consumption. No urban/rural split published (the island is a single ~4,400-person settlement pattern); the national figure is applied to both strata. Table B24 gives an 8-district breakdown if finer geography is ever needed.
bounds_notes: 54.8% of households own a rainwater storage tank, but the census records this as SUPPLEMENTARY storage, not the main supply - explicitly not used to fill OtherUnpiped (that would multiply the real figure ~40x). Packaged/Delivered/Borehole each bounded above by the 1.3% 'other' residual.

source: No source with a household-level water-source breakdown exists. Contextual only: AASS (sole public utility) 2026 drought reporting (GiornaleSM, Tribuna Politica Web) describing heavy dependence on external/surface supplies
mapping_notes: Not fillable. San Marino sits outside EurEau membership, Eurostat/SILC and ISTAT coverage, and no national statistical publication with a source-of-water household table was located. CIA World Factbook / World Bank '100% basic drinking water access' is a modelled JMP-family indicator and cannot resolve source category. The AASS drought narrative implies minimal internal well/spring contribution to SUPPLY, which is a production-side fact, not a household breakdown, so it was not converted into a zero.
bounds_notes: AASS reporting suggests minimal internal well/spring contribution and heavy reliance on imported/surface water - production-side, not household.

mapping_notes: No source of any kind was retrieved. The INSEE DEP-975 dossier returned HTTP 500, no SISPEA page for 975 was reached, and neither Coalition Eau nor ARS surfaced any mention. A ~6,000-population territory with a mature municipal network makes near-100% piped (and therefore near-zero across all four of our columns) the plausible baseline, but that is an assumption with no citation behind it, and the rubric requires either source+url or not_fillable — so not_fillable, with no numbers written.
bounds_notes: Absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. Follow-up: retry the INSEE DEP-975 dossier (the 500 error was transient-looking) and check services.eaufrance.fr for departement 975, which would give the same regulator-proxy basis used for GLP/MTQ/REU and would likely support the same evidence-based zeros.

source: Statisticky urad SR, SODB2021 census, reported via TASR/teraz.sk 22 Mar 2023 ('Vodovod v byte zo spolocneho zdroja ma na Slovensku 1.908.422 bytov')
mapping_notes: SODB2021: 1,908,422 dwellings (85.37%) supplied from a shared/public source -> piped, excluded from our columns. 235,640 (10.5%) from an OWN source (private well) -> Borehole, per rubric treatment of a household's own well with a pump; Slovak 'vlastny zdroj' household supplies are predominantly drilled or dug wells with an electric pump feeding the dwelling's plumbing, so Borehole is the best fit, though the census does not distinguish dug from drilled - a portion of this 10.5 arguably belongs in OtherUnpiped. 45,468 dwellings (~2.0%) have NO water supply -> allocated to OtherUnpiped following the section's suggested mapping (hauled/surface/spring), which is a residual allocation the census itself does not itemise. Categories are dwelling-based, not population-based, and only sum to ~97.9% (the remaining ~2.1% is unstated/not reported).
bounds_notes: Eurostat env_wat_pop gives 90.2% connected to public supply in 2021, consistent with a ~10% self-supply share. Census counts dwellings (may include some vacant/recreational units) rather than people; no urban/rural split published, though the source notes regional variation.
verification: CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 vs SODB2021 (own source 10.5% of dwellings)

source: ARSO environmental indicator 'Access to safe drinking water' (2021)
mapping_notes: Connection-rate proxy: 94.6% of the population is supplied through monitored public water-supply zones (>=50 persons); the 5.4% 'unmonitored' residual is described by ARSO only as 'individual supply or rainwater' (small systems <50 persons), i.e. unsplit. Per rubric rule 4 I allocated the whole residual to the best-supported single category, Borehole (individual household supply from groundwater - groundwater is 63.9% of monitored supply, and individual supply in Slovenia is overwhelmingly own wells/springs), and left OtherUnpiped null rather than double-counting. The rainwater/cistern component (relevant in the karst regions) is therefore folded into Borehole and is unquantified. Small systems serving <50 persons that are piped to the dwelling would arguably count as piped under JMP, which further weakens this fill.
bounds_notes: 5.4% is a CEILING on total self-supply (Borehole + OtherUnpiped combined), not a Borehole-specific measurement. Trend: unmonitored share fell from 7.86% (2004) to 5.36% (2021). No urban/rural split - ARSO reports by supply-zone size only.

source: Department of Statistics (STAT) Sint Maarten, Census 2011 Report, Table G-11 (n=14,922 occupied accommodations)
mapping_notes: Table G-11 main water source: Water supply line 83.5% (piped, excluded per rubric — SXM's network water is desalinated but network-distributed), Bottles of water 7.8% -> Packaged, Water truck 0.5% -> Delivered, Cistern or water well 7.4% -> OtherUnpiped, Other 0.7% left unallocated. The 7.4% is a COMBINED cistern-or-well category the census does not split, so all of it is assigned to OtherUnpiped (rainwater cisterns dominate on an island with no meaningful potable aquifer) and Borehole is left null rather than 0 — an unknown minority of that 7.4% is wells, so the OtherUnpiped value is an upper bound and any true Borehole share is a subset of it, not an addition to it (avoids double-counting, rubric rule 7). Territory-wide single stratum, so the same values are applied to URBAN and RURAL. Column sum check: 83.5 piped + 7.8 + 0.5 + 7.4 + 0.7 other = 99.9, consistent.
bounds_notes: Table G-12 splits wells by PUMP TYPE — windmill / electric pump / no pump. This is one of very few direct household pump-type enumerations found anywhere in the exercise and is directly relevant to the later manual-vs-electric (CIL-resilience) phase; the counts should be extracted from the same PDF. 'Other' 0.7% is unallocated and could belong to any category.

source: Public Utilities Corporation (PUC) Seychelles water pages - 'PUC currently covers 95% of the population's water needs'; households encouraged to add rainwater harvesting as a supplement. NBS 2010/2022 censuses are confirmed to carry housing/water-supply questions (IHSN catalog #4079; NBS download #1555) but nbs.gov.sc geo-blocks non-Seychelles IPs (HTTP 418/403 on every fetch method tried, including proxies).
mapping_notes: NOT FILLED deliberately. The only number available is the PUC claim that it covers 95% of the population's WATER NEEDS - that is a volume/demand-coverage statement, not a share of households whose main drinking source is the network, so the 5% residual cannot be read as a population share, and rubric rule 4 (connection-rate proxy -> residual is a ceiling) does not cleanly apply. The residual is also not attributed by the source to any specific category; the only self-supply the source names is supplementary rainwater harvesting, which by definition is not the main source for those households. Writing 5.0 into OtherUnpiped would convert a utility volume claim into a household-share statistic, so all columns are left null rather than proxy-filled.
bounds_notes: Non-PUC supply is at most ~5% of national water needs; any household self-supply (rainwater tanks, springs) sits inside that. 54%-style tank ownership figures are not available for Seychelles. Borehole use is not mentioned anywhere in the available material - plausibly ~0 on the granitic inner islands (surface dams + desalination), but no source states it, so no 0 was written (rubric rule 3 requires evidence for a zero).

source: Statistical Office SVG, Table 10 'Distribution of Households by Source of Water Supply, 1980–2012', Compendium of Environmental Statistics 2014 p.19, from the 2012 census (n=36,829)
mapping_notes: 2012 categories: Public 83.0% (Piped into Dwelling 68.9 + Yard 11.6 + Standpipe 2.6) -> piped, excluded (standpipes are piped per rubric); Private 13.1% -> OtherUnpiped; Other 3.0% -> OtherUnpiped; Public Well/Tank 0.1% -> Borehole; Not Stated 0.8% unallocated. OtherUnpiped = 13.1 + 3.0 = 16.1. 'Private' is an unbroken catch-all that the section file reads as private cisterns/rain tanks/wells — credible because CWSA's public system is gravity-fed surface water, so anything private is by definition a household's own catchment or well rather than a second network. 'Other' is included on the same reasoning applied to Grenada in this batch (all piped options are separately enumerated, so 'Other' cannot be network water) — the two rows are treated consistently. Borehole = 0.1 from 'Public Well/Tank': the well type is not stated and a public tank is not a borehole at all, so this is a nominal assignment, but at 0.1% it is immaterial either way. Packaged and Delivered null — neither is itemised in this table. Single stratum, applied to both URBAN and RURAL. Sum check: 83.0 piped + 16.1 + 0.1 + 0.8 not stated = 100.0, exact.
bounds_notes: Alternative OtherUnpiped if 'Other' is excluded: 13.1%. The dominant uncertainty is the composition of the 13.1% 'Private' bucket, which is not broken out anywhere in the compendium — it could contain a Delivered component (trucked cistern refills) and a Borehole component. Supply question, not drinking, so a bottled-drinking population is invisible; given AIA (60.7% bottled) and VGB (80.5% bottled), Packaged for VCT is likely materially above zero and simply unmeasured.

source: HumVenezuela national humanitarian survey 2023 (~11,000 households, 20 states), reported via Efecto Cocuyo 27 Jan 2024; supplemented by OVSP 12-city surveys (Mar 2023, Apr 2022) and INE Censo 2011.
mapping_notes: NOT FILLED, per rubric rule 5. Every HumVenezuela figure is a MULTI-RESPONSE 'share of population reporting use of this alternative source' - households use several simultaneously and the categories sum to well over 100 (86% used at least one alternative source in 2023). Inserting them would break rubric rule 7 (mutual exclusivity) and would inflate total unpiped population far past 100% of the zone. The INE Censo 2011 fallback the prompt allows does NOT rescue the row either: the only national census number available in the section file is '>95% via acueducto/pipes', which is a PIPED share with an unsplit <5% residual - it yields no main-source breakdown for any of our four columns, and the two subnational splits (Miranda 93% aqueduct / 2% cistern truck; Tachira 89% aqueduct) are single-state and cannot stand in for national urban/rural. INE 2011 is also pre-crisis and would misrepresent 2023 conditions by a wide margin, so it was rejected as a fill even with a dated flag. All quantities preserved in bounds_notes.
bounds_notes: HumVenezuela 2023 (% of population reporting USE, multi-response, NOT main source): bottled/botellones 48.9; rainwater harvesting 20.9 (up from 0.9 in 2022); underground wells 18.2 (up from 10.7 in 2022); tanker trucks 16.9; springs/rivers/streams 12.1; 86.0 used at least one alternative source (75.9 in 2022). OVSP Mar 2023 (12 cities): 20.3% receive water from deep wells (private/community/mixed); 92.3% store water. OVSP Apr 2022 (12 cities): only 27.1% have continuous piped service; 22.7% pay for tanker-truck water; 47% store water. INE Censo 2011 (pre-crisis baseline): >95% national on acueducto; Miranda 93% aqueduct / 2% cistern truck; Tachira 89% aqueduct. ENCOVI (UCAB) 2022-2025: 78-80% aqueduct access, source-mix table not retrieved. Directionally: true Venezuelan Borehole and Delivered shares are certainly non-trivial and rising, so leaving nulls understates unpiped use - a targeted ENCOVI main-source table would be the highest-value follow-up in this batch.

source: Government of the Virgin Islands, Virgin Islands 2010 Population and Housing Census Report, Table 26 'Main Source of Drinking Water' (n=10,830 households), pp.22–24
mapping_notes: Filled from the DRINKING table (Table 26) per rubric rule 1. Bottled Water 80.5% -> Packaged. OtherUnpiped = 16.2% = Private piped into dwelling filtered 8.7 + Private piped unfiltered 3.8 + Private catchments not piped 1.8 + Spring 1.8 + Private dug well 0.1 + Public dug well 0.0. The private-piped categories are cistern water: Table 24 labels the same category explicitly as 'Private piped/cistern', so the delivery method is piped but the SOURCE is rainwater catchment, which stays in our columns per rubric. Borehole = 0, deliberately DIFFERING from the section file's suggested mapping: the section proposed Borehole = dug wells ~0.1%, but the rubric assigns dug/traditional wells to OtherUnpiped and reserves Borehole for drilled tubewells, and the census offers no drilled-well category at all — so the 0.1% dug wells go to OtherUnpiped and Borehole is an evidence-based 0. Delivered = 0: the drinking table has no tanker option, and the general-supply table caps truck-borne at 0.1%, so 0 is right to within a tenth without mixing tables. Excluded as piped: Public piped into dwelling 1.6% + Standpipe 0.1%. 'Public & Private piped' 0.6% is excluded as mixed-source. Single stratum, applied to both URBAN and RURAL. Sum check: 80.5 + 16.2 + 1.7 piped + 0.6 mixed = 99.0, with ~1% rounding/not-stated.
bounds_notes: Household-supply table (Table 24, general use, NOT used for the fill): Public piped 48.1%, Private piped/cistern 31.9%, Combined 15.9%, Catchments not piped 1.2%, Spring/Well 1.0%, Truck-borne 0.1%. The supply-vs-drinking contrast is the sharpest in the whole batch and is the evidence base for rejecting a rainwater fill for Bermuda: cisterns supply a third of households but bottled is the drinking source for four in five. Upper bound on OtherUnpiped is 16.8% if the 0.6% 'Public & Private piped' is treated as private cistern. By-island variation: Virgin Gorda 84% bottled vs Anegada 52%. VGB is dropped by drop_small_island_nations in the model (rubric rule 10) but the row is produced for dataset completeness. No 2021 census report published yet.

source: US Census Bureau, 2010 Census of Population and Housing (Island Areas), table HBG41 'Source of Water' (n=55,901 units) and table HBG42 'Purchase of Water from Water Vendor' (n=43,214 responding occupied units), DECENNIALVI2010, geography 0400000US78. Counts pulled directly from the Census API 2026-08-07; supersedes the earlier low-confidence EPA/PMC secondary figures.
mapping_notes: HBG41 full table: public system only 16,480 = 29.48%; public system AND cistern 9,784 = 17.50%; cistern/tanks/drums only 28,606 = 51.17%; public standpipe 78 = 0.14%; some other source 953 = 1.70%. Sums to 99.99. OtherUnpiped = cistern-only 51.17 (rainwater cisterns are the classic OtherUnpiped category). EXCLUDED as piped: public-only 29.48 + public standpipe 0.14 (standpipes are piped per rubric) + hybrid public+cistern 17.50. HYBRID DECISION: the 17.50% is counted piped-primary for consistency across the four US island areas, but this is the least comfortable of the four - USVI public supply is desalinated and expensive and many hybrid households run principally off the cistern, so the real OtherUnpiped is plausibly closer to the 68.67 ceiling than to 51.17. Borehole left NULL rather than 0: HBG41 has no well category, but USGS records groundwater as 18% of total USVI water use with 55% of that going to rural domestic supply, so private domestic wells demonstrably exist - they must be hiding inside 'some other source' (1.70%), which therefore bounds Borehole rather than zeroing it. For the same reason the 1.70% was NOT added to OtherUnpiped (unlike the ASM/GUM/MNP 'other' lines, where no independent evidence of wells existed). PACKAGED AND DELIVERED DELIBERATELY NOT FILLED: HBG42 (store 59.01%, delivery vendor 7.62%, both 6.51%, none 26.85%) is a separate PURCHASE question on a smaller denominator - it asks whether the household buys water, not what its main drinking source is, and store-purchasers overwhelmingly also have a cistern or public connection, so the categories are not mutually exclusive with HBG41 (rubric rules 5 and 7). The PMC 82%-bottled figure is a 399-household convenience survey (rubric rule 6). Both are in bounds_notes. Household supply question, not drinking-specific. Territory-wide, no urban/rural split; values written to both strata. Rubric rule 10: VIR is dropped by drop_small_island_nations in the model, but the row is produced for dataset completeness. | VERIFIER: 51.17% universe is total HOUSING UNITS (55,901), not occupied households (43,214); cistern-only by occupancy not published. A further 17.5% are public-system-AND-cistern.
bounds_notes: HBG42 purchase table (n=43,214, multi-response-ish, NOT filled): purchased from a delivery vendor 3,294 = 7.62%; purchased from a supermarket/grocery store 25,502 = 59.01%; purchased from both 2,813 = 6.51%; no water purchased 11,605 = 26.85%. So 65.52% buy water at a store and 14.13% buy from a delivery vendor - these are ceilings on Packaged and Delivered respectively, not main-source shares. PMC 2019 household survey (n=399, convenience): bottled water was the primary drinking source for 82% - consistent in direction with the 65.5% store-purchase ceiling but too small/non-representative to fill from. Borehole ceiling = 1.70 ('some other source'). OtherUnpiped ceiling = 68.67 if the 17.50% public+cistern hybrid were resolved as cistern-primary. EPA Region 2 secondary figures (~95% of homes collect/store water in cisterns; <32% piped connection) are consistent with the census 68.67% cistern-any share only if 'collect/store' includes supplementary storage.
verification: CONFIRMED 2026-08-08 vs Census 2010 DP summary file vi95 (28,606/55,901 = 51.17%)
